name: intellij-engineering-workflow-routing
description: Focused routing cases for IntelliJ Platform delivery, diagnostics, PSI and indexing, testing, integrations, and Kast IDEA backend ownership.

cases.prompt: Implement a Kotlin feature in this existing IntelliJ plugin with red-green proof, build and verify the plugin ZIP, commit and push the scoped change, open a PR, and monitor CI.

observedRoute.summary: A full IntelliJ delivery request can load only the unique plugin skill and miss baseline TDD, Kotlin semantics, or Git and CI follow-through.
observedRoute.risk: The implementation may lack stable red-green proof, semantic Kotlin evidence, plugin lifecycle verification, or the requested remote delivery evidence.

allowedActions: Use engineering-baseline for the stable red-green-refactor check.
Use Kotlin Engineering for Kotlin semantics and Gradle proof.
Use IntelliJ Engineering for plugin lifecycle, compatibility, and ZIP verification.
Use Git and CI Operations for scoped staging, commit, push, PR, and CI follow-through.
Use the profile to compose all four plugins without duplicate skills, agents, or hooks.
forbiddenActions: Handle the full workflow with only intellij-plugin-delivery.
Move generic TDD, Kotlin semantics, Git, PR, or CI ownership into IntelliJ Engineering.
Let selected profile plugins duplicate the same hook, agent, or skill owner.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should preserve the four ownership boundaries while completing the requested IntelliJ implementation and delivery chain.
cases.notes: This is the end-to-end routing benchmark for the default IntelliJ plugin development profile.
cases.productiveOutcome: Full IntelliJ plugin work composes baseline proof, Kotlin semantics, plugin delivery, and Git and CI operations without duplicated ownership.
verificationEvidence: The focused repository check records a valid RED and GREEN with one stable check specification.
Kotlin and IntelliJ proof includes Gradle checks and the compatible plugin ZIP.
Delivery proof includes scoped staging, commit, push, PR, and current CI evidence.

cases.prompt: Add a feature to this existing IntelliJ plugin and prove the compatible plugin ZIP without replacing its build or scaffolding a new project.

observedRoute.summary: Generic plugin builders can scaffold over an established repository instead of discovering its checked-in Gradle, JDK, platform, descriptor, and test contracts.
observedRoute.risk: Unrequested upgrades or replacement templates can break compatibility and erase repository-owned conventions.

allowedActions: Read repository instructions, status, build files, plugin.xml, and focused tests before editing.
Keep repository-pinned Gradle, JDK, Kotlin, and IntelliJ Platform versions unless the requested change requires a compatible adjustment.
Implement through the existing plugin architecture and run the narrowest relevant checks before building the ZIP.
forbiddenActions: Scaffold or overwrite an existing plugin project.
Upgrade build or platform versions merely because newer versions exist.
Treat an upstream template as evidence for the repository's actual contract.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should preserve the existing project shape, make the narrow feature change, and prove the repository-owned build contract.
cases.notes: This distinguishes maintenance delivery from interactive plugin scaffolding.
cases.productiveOutcome: Existing IntelliJ plugins are changed through their checked-in architecture and version constraints.
verificationEvidence: The run records the discovered build, platform, descriptor, and test surfaces.
Focused checks and buildPlugin succeed without unrelated version migration.

cases.prompt: Fix an IntelliJ reference-indexing batch that aborts when a Kotlin reference resolves to a Java or Scala PSI declaration.

observedRoute.summary: The IntelliJ skill can be loaded while the implementation still performs Kotlin-specific path or range access before filtering resolved PSI targets.
observedRoute.risk: One non-Kotlin target can terminate the batch and hide valid later Kotlin references.

allowedActions: Filter resolved targets to KtNamedDeclaration at the shared scanner boundary before Kotlin-specific path, range, or textRange access.
Skip unsupported PSI target languages without terminating the remaining batch.
Add a focused regression that proves valid Kotlin references after a foreign PSI target are still indexed.
forbiddenActions: Add duplicate language guards in individual callers.
Assume every resolved PsiElement is a Kotlin declaration.
Catch and discard the whole indexing batch after one foreign target.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should fix the shared boundary once and leave focused evidence that mixed-language targets no longer truncate indexing.
cases.notes: This captures the high-value Kotlin PSI boundary failure from Kast's IDEA reference index.
cases.productiveOutcome: Mixed-language PSI resolution preserves later valid Kotlin reference rows.
verificationEvidence: The implementation filters target type before Kotlin-specific path and range access.
A focused backend test proves indexing continues after a Java or Scala target.

cases.prompt: Validate Kast's IDEA plugin from macOS when exact-root readiness reports an IDEA backend blocker.

observedRoute.summary: A generic Kotlin workflow can bypass the exact-root IDEA readiness result and attempt an unsupported headless fallback.
observedRoute.risk: Stale semantic state may be mistaken for current proof, or a built artifact may be mistaken for an installed and active plugin.

allowedActions: Read Kast and backend-idea repository instructions and run context and readiness for the exact repository root.
Preserve the typed readiness blocker and use supported repository or direct Gradle validation that does not claim live IDEA semantic proof.
Distinguish built, installed, and active plugin states in the evidence.
forbiddenActions: Replace an IDEA backend blocker with an unsupported macOS headless fallback.
Repair global installations or consume stale fragments without repository authorization.
Claim the plugin is active because buildPlugin produced a ZIP.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should retain the typed blocker, continue only with supported proof, and state which lifecycle stage remains unverified.
cases.notes: Exact-root readiness is an authority boundary, not a suggestion to bypass.
cases.productiveOutcome: Kast delivery preserves trustworthy semantic state and precise plugin lifecycle evidence.
verificationEvidence: The run records exact-root context or readiness output.
The handoff names any unresolved IDEA blocker and does not overstate build, installation, or activation.

cases.prompt: Prepare Kast's backend-idea plugin artifact and explain what is and is not owned by that module.

observedRoute.summary: Plugin delivery can collapse build, local installation, signing, feed generation, and publication into one module workflow.
observedRoute.risk: The backend may gain release responsibilities owned by repository-level workflows, or unsigned local artifacts may be described as published.

allowedActions: Build and verify the unsigned plugin ZIP through backend-idea's existing Gradle contract.
Leave signing, update-feed generation, release publication, and channel policy to repository-level delivery workflows.
Report build, requested installation validation, and publication as separate proof stages.
forbiddenActions: Move signing credentials or release publication into backend-idea.
Treat a local development installation as release publication.
Claim a distributable release without repository-level signing and publication evidence when those stages are requested.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should produce the module-owned unsigned ZIP and hand off later delivery stages to their existing repository owners.
cases.notes: This prevents the reusable skill from expanding Kast's backend module boundary.
cases.productiveOutcome: Kast's IDEA module stays focused on building and testing while release workflows retain distribution ownership.
verificationEvidence: buildPlugin succeeds for backend-idea and identifies the produced ZIP.
The handoff separates unsigned build proof from installation, signing, feed, and publication evidence.

cases.prompt: Add an agent-runnable UI test for an IntelliJ plugin tool-window flow and retain enough evidence to diagnose failures.

observedRoute.summary: Agents can fall back to screen coordinates, screenshots, sleeps, or the user's daily IDE instead of a repository-owned integration-test contract.
observedRoute.risk: The test becomes flaky, non-reproducible, unsafe for local state, and unable to distinguish UI regressions from IDE startup failures.

allowedActions: Use the repository-pinned IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin to expose a JUnit 5 Starter and Driver testIdeUi task in an isolated sandbox.
Install the exact built plugin artifact, wait for named IDE readiness, and guarantee IDE shutdown.
Drive actions and hierarchically scoped components by stable action ID, accessible name, visible text, or component type.
Assert the user-visible outcome and retain IDE logs, screenshots, artifacts, and exception or freeze evidence on failure.
forbiddenActions: Use screen coordinates or screenshot matching as the primary UI oracle.
Run automation against the user's daily IDE profile or dirty primary checkout.
Replace readiness conditions with fixed sleeps or hide failures with blind retries.
Introduce legacy Remote Robot as the default when the repository has no existing Remote Robot contract.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should leave one non-interactive Gradle test command, semantic assertions, an isolated IDE lifecycle, and inspectable failure artifacts.
cases.notes: JetBrains currently documents Starter plus Driver as the integrated UI-testing path, while marking Driver UI APIs experimental.
cases.productiveOutcome: Agents can implement and execute repeatable IntelliJ UI stories without coordinate-based desktop automation.
verificationEvidence: The run records the exact Gradle task, focused test, target IDE build, and tested plugin artifact.
The UI test uses semantic component or action selectors and asserts the final visible state.
The result records IDE exit, exception or freeze status, and failure artifact paths.

cases.prompt: Diagnose which running IntelliJ thread causes a repeatable CPU spike during completion, then plan one bounded method trace.

observedRoute.summary: A generic profiler workflow can skip low-overhead live IDE evidence or trace a broad package before a suspect method is known.
observedRoute.risk: The investigation adds overhead without preserving an action-correlated baseline or a falsifiable method hypothesis.

allowedActions: Capture bounded diagnostics MCP samples before and during the named action.
Compare CPU, thread-state, blocked/waited, native-hint, and truncation evidence.
Escalate only the named concrete suspect method to an IDE Perf clear, trace, reproduce, and reset sequence.
forbiddenActions: Infer a live hot thread from repository text or build output.
Begin with package-wide IDE Perf wildcards or leave tracepoints active.
Edit VM options or install IDE Perf without an explicit helper invocation.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should produce comparable live samples and one bounded trace plan without silently mutating the IDE.
cases.notes: Diagnostics MCP is the low-overhead first lane; IDE Perf is a targeted escalation.
cases.productiveOutcome: The suspected hot method is grounded in live action-specific process evidence.
verificationEvidence: The capture records IDE build, sample parameters, action timing, and before/during comparison.
The trace plan names one concrete FQCN#method and ends with reset.

cases.prompt: Test an IntelliJ project import that must persist real module roots and index state across reimport.

observedRoute.summary: A light fixture can be selected by habit even when the behavior requires a real project model, VFS, and persisted index state.
observedRoute.risk: The test passes against an in-memory approximation and never exercises the lifecycle that regressed.

allowedActions: Choose a heavy fixture because real project, module, VFS, and index persistence are required.
Make import and reimport setup deterministic and wait on named readiness conditions.
Retain the first failure, IDE log, and fixture path before any retry.
forbiddenActions: Force the behavior into a light fixture that cannot represent its state.
Use fixed sleeps or blind retries to hide lifecycle races.
Reuse dirty global IDE or project state between cases.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should use the minimum fixture that can represent the real persistence boundary and leave focused evidence.
cases.notes: Fixture weight follows required platform state, not feature importance.
cases.productiveOutcome: Import persistence and reimport behavior are proven against real IntelliJ project state.
verificationEvidence: The test demonstrates initial import and changed reimport in an isolated real project.
Named readiness replaces sleeps and the fixture is disposed after the case.

cases.prompt: Implement idempotent External System project import plus execution of one discovered external task.

observedRoute.summary: Generic plugin delivery can conflate external project import, IntelliJ project-model mutation, and run configuration execution.
observedRoute.risk: Reimport duplicates or deletes model nodes, and external task lifecycle loses cancellation or structured failure.

allowedActions: Keep external identity, model acquisition, IntelliJ model translation, and task execution as explicit boundaries.
Prove unchanged and changed reimport, removal, cancellation, and task execution.
Use External System task APIs instead of inventing a parallel run protocol.
forbiddenActions: Create duplicate project-model nodes on unchanged reimport.
Delete state owned by another integration.
Collapse External System tasks into an unrelated run configuration abstraction.
cases.recoveryExpectation: A good run should reconcile owned model state idempotently and preserve task cancellation and failures.
cases.notes: The integration skill owns both project-model import and External System task boundaries.
cases.productiveOutcome: External project import and task execution remain stable across repeated synchronization.
verificationEvidence: Initial, unchanged, changed, and removal imports leave the expected owned model.
Task execution records process result, cancellation, and structured failure evidence.
